text: Number of complexes from the following with even number of unpaired "$\mathrm{d}$" electrons is $________$ $[\mathrm{V}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{6}]^{3+},[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{6}]^{2+},[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{6}]^{3+},[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{6}]^{3+},[\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{6}]^{2+}$ [Given atomic numbers: $\mathrm{V}=23,\mathrm{Cr}=24,\mathrm{Fe}=26,\mathrm{Ni}=28,\mathrm{Cu}=29$]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Paired electrons come in twos, so the number of unpaired electrons has the same parity as the number of d electrons.

$[\mathrm{V}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{6}]{}^{3+}$: $\mathrm{V}{}^{3+}$ is $3d^{2}$, $t_{2g}^{2}$, 2 unpaired electrons (even).

$[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{6}]{}^{2+}$: $\mathrm{Cr}{}^{2+}$ is $3d^{4}$; $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ is a weak-field ligand, so $t_{2g}^{3}e_{g}^{1}$, 4 unpaired electrons (even).

$[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{6}]{}^{3+}$: $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}$ is $3d^{5}$, $t_{2g}^{3}e_{g}^{2}$, 5 unpaired electrons (odd).

$[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{6}]{}^{3+}$: Ni is $3d^{8}4s^{2}$, so $\mathrm{Ni}{}^{3+}$ is $3d^{7}$, $t_{2g}^{5}e_{g}^{2}$, 3 unpaired electrons (odd); a low-spin $t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{1}$ arrangement would also be odd.

$[\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{6}]{}^{2+}$: $\mathrm{Cu}{}^{2+}$ is $3d^{9}$, $t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{3}$, 1 unpaired electron (odd).

Only the V(III) and Cr(II) complexes have an even number of unpaired d electrons, so the number is 2.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift

text: What will be the decreasing order of basic strength of the following conjugate bases? ${}^{-}\mathrm{OH},\mathrm{R}\mathrm{O}–,\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{CO}\mathrm{O}–,\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A base is stronger when its conjugate acid is weaker. The conjugate acids are $\mathrm{ROH}$, $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{COOH}$ and $\mathrm{HCl}$.

Alcohols are weaker acids than water because the electron-releasing alkyl group ($+I$) increases the electron density on oxygen; hence $\mathrm{RO}{}^{-}$ accepts a proton more readily than $\mathrm{OH}{}^{-}$.

In $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{COO}{}^{-}$ the negative charge is delocalised over two oxygen atoms by resonance, so acetate is a much weaker base than $\mathrm{OH}{}^{-}$.

$\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$ is the conjugate base of the strong acid $\mathrm{HCl}$; its charge sits on a large, electronegative atom, so it is the weakest base.

$\mathrm{RO}{}^{-}>\mathrm{OH}{}^{-}>\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{COO}{}^{-}>\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift

text:
Given below are two statements :

Statements I : Acidity of $α$-hydrogens of aldehydes and ketones is responsible for Aldol reaction.

Statement II : Reaction between benzaldehyde and ethanal will NOT give Cross - Aldol product.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let's analyze the given statements in detail:

Statement I: Acidity of $α$-hydrogens of aldehydes and ketones is responsible for Aldol reaction.

This statement is correct. The presence of acidic $α$-hydrogens in aldehydes and ketones makes it possible for these compounds to undergo deprotonation, forming enolates. These enolates can then attack the carbonyl carbon of another aldehyde or ketone, leading to the formation of the Aldol product. Therefore, the acidity of the $α$-hydrogens is crucial for the Aldol reaction.

Statement II: Reaction between benzaldehyde and ethanal will NOT give Cross-Aldol product.

This statement is incorrect. Benzaldehyde (which lacks an $α$-hydrogen) can indeed react with ethanal (which has an $α$-hydrogen) in a Cross-Aldol reaction. In a Cross-Aldol reaction, one molecule (ethanal) forms an enolate and reacts with another molecule (benzaldehyde), resulting in the formation of a Cross-Aldol product.

Based on these explanations, the most appropriate answer is:

Option B

Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift

text: In the precipitation of the iron group (III) in qualitative analysis, ammonium chloride is added before adding ammonium hydroxide to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In qualitative analysis, the precipitation of the iron group (III) requires careful control of conditions to ensure selective precipitation of the desired ions. Ammonium chloride is added before ammonium hydroxide to achieve this control effectively.

Let's analyze the options to understand why ammonium chloride is used:

Option A: decrease concentration of $\mathrm{OH}^{-}$ ions

This option is correct. Adding ammonium chloride ($\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{Cl}$) introduces a common ion effect, where the concentration of $\mathrm{OH}^{-}$ ions is reduced due to the formation of $\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{OH}$. This reaction can be represented as:

$\mathrm{NH}_{4}^{+}+\mathrm{OH}^{-}\leftrightarrow \mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{OH}$

By reducing the concentration of $\mathrm{OH}^{-}$ ions, it prevents the premature precipitation of hydroxides of metals that might otherwise not selectively precipitate in the desired group.

Option B: increase concentration of $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$ ions

While it is true that ammonium chloride increases the concentration of $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$ ions, this is not the primary reason for its addition in this context. The focus is more on regulating $\mathrm{OH}^{-}$ ion concentration.

Option C: prevent interference by phosphate ions

This is not relevant in the context of adding ammonium chloride, as the main idea behind adding ammonium chloride is to control the $\mathrm{OH}^{-}$ ion concentration rather than dealing directly with phosphate ions.

Option D: increase concentration of $\mathrm{NH}_{4}^{+}$ ions

While ammonium chloride does increase the concentration of $\mathrm{NH}_{4}^{+}$ ions, which in turn helps in maintaining the $\mathrm{OH}^{-}$ concentration at a lower level, this is again a secondary consideration to the primary goal of controlling the $\mathrm{OH}^{-}$ ion concentration to ensure selective precipitation.

Therefore, the correct answer is:

Option A: decrease concentration of $\mathrm{OH}^{-}$ ions
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift

text: The element which shows only one oxidation state other than its elemental form is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The element among the given options that shows only one oxidation state other than its elemental form is Scandium.

Explanation:

Nickel (Ni) can have multiple oxidation states, including +2 and +3, with +2 being the most common.

Titanium (Ti) also shows various oxidation states, most commonly +4 and +2, due to its ability to lose electrons from both its 3d and 4s subshells.

Cobalt (Co) commonly exists in the +2 and +3 oxidation states, among others, due to electron transitions in its 3d orbitals.

Scandium (Sc), however, primarily exhibits a +3 oxidation state in its compounds (excluding its 0 state in the elemental form). This is because scandium has an electronic configuration of [Ar]$3d^{1}4s^{2}$, and it loses all three outer electrons to achieve a stable configuration, resulting in a +3 oxidation state. It does not commonly exhibit other oxidation states because removing more than three electrons would require removing electrons from the very stable noble gas core configuration ([Ar]), which is energetically unfavorable.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D: Scandium.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift

text: Which of the following is the correct structure of L-Glucose?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In the Fischer projection of D-glucose the OH groups at C-2, C-3, C-4 and C-5 lie on the right, left, right and right respectively.

L-Glucose is the mirror image (enantiomer) of D-glucose, so the configuration at every chiral centre is reversed: OH at C-2 on the left, C-3 on the right, C-4 on the left and C-5 on the left.

Structure (D) has exactly this arrangement.


[IMG]

Structure (A) inverts only C-5 (right, left, right, left); it is a diastereomer of D-glucose (L-idose), not its mirror image.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text:
Number of molecules/ions from the following in which the central atom is involved in $\mathrm{sp}^{3}$ hybridization is $________$.

$\mathrm{NO}_{3}^{-},\mathrm{BCl}_{3},\mathrm{ClO}_{2}^{-},\mathrm{ClO}_{3}^{-}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To determine the number of molecules/ions in which the central atom is involved in $\mathrm{sp}^{3}$ hybridization, we must analyze the hybridization state for each central atom. Hybridization is typically determined by the number of sigma bonds and lone pairs on the central atom.

Let's evaluate each molecule/ion:

1. $\mathrm{NO}_{3}^{-}$:

The central atom is nitrogen (N). In $\mathrm{NO}_{3}^{-}$, nitrogen forms three sigma bonds with oxygen atoms and has no lone pairs. Using the formula for hybridization:

 Number of hybrid orbitals = number of sigma bonds + number of lone pairs

For $\mathrm{NO}_{3}^{-}$: $3+0=3$ hybrid orbitals. Therefore, nitrogen is $\mathrm{sp}^{2}$ hybridized.

2. $\mathrm{BCl}_{3}$:

The central atom is boron (B). In $\mathrm{BCl}_{3}$, boron forms three sigma bonds with chlorine atoms and has no lone pairs. Using the same formula:

 For $\mathrm{BCl}_{3}$: $3+0=3$ hybrid orbitals. Therefore, boron is $\mathrm{sp}^{2}$ hybridized.

3. $\mathrm{ClO}_{2}^{-}$:

The central atom is chlorine (Cl). In $\mathrm{ClO}_{2}^{-}$, chlorine forms two sigma bonds with oxygen atoms and has two lone pairs. Therefore,:

 For $\mathrm{ClO}_{2}^{-}$: $2+2=4$ hybrid orbitals. Thus, chlorine is $\mathrm{sp}^{3}$ hybridized.

4. $\mathrm{ClO}_{3}^{-}$:

The central atom is chlorine (Cl). In $\mathrm{ClO}_{3}^{-}$, chlorine forms three sigma bonds with oxygen atoms and has one lone pair. Therefore,:

 For $\mathrm{ClO}_{3}^{-}$: $3+1=4$ hybrid orbitals. Thus, chlorine is $\mathrm{sp}^{3}$ hybridized.

Based on the analysis, the molecules/ions $\mathrm{ClO}_{2}^{-}$ and $\mathrm{ClO}_{3}^{-}$ have their central atoms involved in $\mathrm{sp}^{3}$ hybridization.

Therefore, the total number is 2.

Thus, the correct option is Option A.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift

text: The Molarity (M) of an aqueous solution containing $5.85\mathrm{g}$ of $\mathrm{NaCl}$ in $500\mathrm{mL}$ water is : (Given : Molar Mass $\mathrm{Na}:23$ and $\mathrm{Cl}:35.5\mathrm{gmol}^{-1}$)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To find the molarity of the aqueous solution, we need to calculate the number of moles of NaCl and then divide it by the volume of the solution in liters.

First, determine the molar mass of NaCl:

$\text{Molar mass of NaCl}=\text{Molar mass of Na}+\text{Molar mass of Cl}=23+35.5=58.5\text{g/mol}$

Next, calculate the moles of NaCl:

$\text{Moles of NaCl}=\frac{5.85\text{g}}{58.5\text{g/mol}}=0.1\text{mol}$

Now, convert the volume of the solution from milliliters to liters:

$500\text{mL}=0.500\text{L}$

Finally, calculate the molarity (M), which is the number of moles of solute per liter of solution:

$M=\frac{\text{Moles of NaCl}}{\text{Volume of solution in liters}}=\frac{0.1\text{mol}}{0.500\text{L}}=0.2\text{M}$

Therefore, the molarity of the solution is 0.2 M. The correct option is D.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift

text: Which among the following is incorrect statement?
options: The electromeric effect is a temporary effect
Hydrogen ion $(\mathrm{H}^{+})$ shows negative electromeric effect
The organic compound shows electromeric effect in the presence of the reagent only.
Electromeric effect dominates over inductive effect
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let's analyze each statement to determine which is incorrect:

Option A: The electromeric effect is a temporary effect.

This statement is correct. The electromeric effect is indeed a temporary effect that occurs in the presence of a reagent and disappears when the reagent is removed.

Option B: Hydrogen ion $(\mathrm{H}^{+})$ shows negative electromeric effect.

To understand this, let's define the electromeric effect. The electromeric effect involves the transfer of electron pairs within a molecule in the presence of an attacking reagent. There are two types of electromeric effects: the positive electromeric effect ($E^{+}$) and the negative electromeric effect ($E^{-}$). A positive electromeric effect occurs when electrons are transferred towards the reagent, while a negative electromeric effect occurs when electrons are transferred away from the reagent.

Since a hydrogen ion $(\mathrm{H}^{+})$ is an electron-deficient species (it lacks electrons), it would generally induce the transfer of electrons towards itself, resulting in a positive electromeric effect. Hence, this statement is incorrect.

Option C: The organic compound shows electromeric effect in the presence of the reagent only.

This statement is correct. The electromeric effect is observed only in the presence of an attacking reagent. Once the reagent is removed, the effect ceases to exist.

Option D: Electromeric effect dominates over inductive effect.

This statement is correct. The electromeric effect generally has a stronger influence on the electronic distribution within a molecule compared to the inductive effect, especially when both effects are present simultaneously.

Therefore, the incorrect statement is:

Option B: Hydrogen ion $(\mathrm{H}^{+})$ shows negative electromeric effect.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift

text: One of the commonly used electrode is calomel electrode. Under which of the following categories, calomel electrode comes?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A calomel electrode consists of mercury in contact with sparingly soluble mercury(I) chloride (calomel) and a solution of chloride ions (KCl):

$\mathrm{Hg}(\mathrm{l})|\mathrm{Hg}{}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}(\mathrm{s})|\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}(\mathrm{aq})$

Electrode reaction: $\mathrm{Hg}{}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}(\mathrm{s})+2\mathrm{e}{}^{-}\longrightarrow 2\mathrm{Hg}(\mathrm{l})+2\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}(\mathrm{aq})$

The metal (Hg) is in contact with its insoluble salt ($\mathrm{Hg}{}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}$), which is in equilibrium with the anion of that salt ($\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$), and the electrode potential depends on $[\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}]$. This is a metal–insoluble salt–anion electrode, of the same type as $\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{s})|\mathrm{AgCl}(\mathrm{s})|\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}(\mathrm{aq})$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift

text: Which of the following nitrogen containing compound does not give Lassaigne's test ?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In Lassaigne's test, nitrogen is detected only after it combines with the carbon of the compound during sodium fusion to give sodium cyanide, which then gives Prussian blue with $\mathrm{FeSO}{}_{4}$ and acidified $\mathrm{FeCl}{}_{3}$:

$\mathrm{Na}+\mathrm{C}+\mathrm{N}{}^{\Delta }\mathrm{NaCN}$

Glycine ($\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{NCH}{}_{2}\mathrm{COOH}$), phenylhydrazine ($\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{NHNH}{}_{2}$) and urea ($\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{NCONH}{}_{2}$) contain both carbon and nitrogen, so they form $\mathrm{NaCN}$ and give the test.

Hydrazine ($\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}$) contains nitrogen but no carbon, so no $\mathrm{NaCN}$ forms and the test is negative.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift

text: What pressure (bar) of $\mathrm{H}_{2}$ would be required to make emf of hydrogen electrode zero in pure water at $25^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$ ?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The hydrogen electrode reaction, written as a reduction, is $2~\mathrm{H}{}^{+}\qquad (\mathrm{aq})+2\mathrm{e}{}^{-}\longrightarrow \mathrm{H}{}_{2}(\mathrm{g})$ with $E^{\circ }=0$ V.

$E=E^{\circ }-\dfrac{0.059}{2}\log \dfrac{p_{\mathrm{H}{}_{2}}}{[\mathrm{H}{}^{+}]^{2}}$

In pure water at $25^{\circ }\text{C}$, $[\mathrm{H}{}^{+}]=10^{-7}\text{M}$. Since $E^{\circ }=0$, $E=0$ requires the log term to be zero:

$\dfrac{p_{\mathrm{H}{}_{2}}}{[\mathrm{H}{}^{+}]^{2}}=1\Rightarrow p_{\mathrm{H}{}_{2}}=(10^{-7})^{2}=10^{-14}\text{bar}$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift

$2.5\mathrm{g}$ of a non-volatile, non-electrolyte is dissolved in $100\mathrm{g}$ of water at $25^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$. The solution showed a boiling point elevation by $2^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$. Assuming the solute concentration is negligible with respect to the solvent concentration, the vapor pressure of the resulting aqueous solution is $_________$ $\mathrm{mm}$ of $\mathrm{Hg}$ (nearest integer)

[Given : Molal boiling point elevation constant of water $(\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{b}})=0.52\mathrm{K}.\mathrm{kg}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$, $1\mathrm{atm}$ pressure $=760\mathrm{mm}$ of $\mathrm{Hg}$, molar mass of water $=18\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}]$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Molal boiling point elevation constant of water ($K_{b}$) = 0.52 K.kg.mol$^{-1}$

1 atm = 760 mm Hg

Molar mass of water = 18 g.mol$^{-1}$

First, we calculate the molality (m) of the solution using the boiling point elevation formula:

$\Delta T_{b}=K_{b}\times m$

From the problem, we know:

$2=0.52\times m$

Solving for m:

$m=\frac{2}{0.52}\approx 3.846\text{mol/kg}$

Next, considering the solution is highly diluted, we use the formula for relative lowering of vapor pressure:

$\frac{\Delta P}{P^{0}}=\frac{n_{\text{solute}}}{n_{\text{solvent}}}$

Given that molality (m) is defined as the number of moles of solute per kilogram of solvent:

$\frac{\Delta P}{P^{0}}=\frac{m}{1000}\times M_{solvent}$

Substitute the known values:

$\Delta P=P^{0}\times \frac{m}{1000}\times M_{solvent}$

$=760\times \frac{3.846}{1000}\times 18$

$=52.615\text{mm Hg}$

Therefore, the vapor pressure of the solution:

$P_{solution}=P^{0}-\Delta P$

$=760-52.615$

$\approx 707.385\text{mm Hg}$

Rounding to the nearest integer, the vapor pressure of the aqueous solution is 707 mm Hg.

text: The de-Broglie's wavelength of an electron in the $4^{\text{th}}$ orbit is $________$ $π\mathrm{a}_{0}$. ($\mathrm{a}_{0}=$ Bohr's radius)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The de-Broglie wavelength of an electron can be expressed through its relationship with the principal quantum number $n$ in a Bohr orbit. According to de Broglie, the wavelength $λ$ of an electron moving in an orbit can be related to its momentum. However, when considering an electron in an atom, specifically within the Bohr model, we can relate the de-Broglie wavelength to the circumference of the orbit it moves in. The formula representing the de Broglie wavelength of an electron in the $n^{\text{th}}$ orbit of a hydrogen-like atom is:

$λ_{n}=\frac{2πr_{n}}{n}$

where

$λ_{n}$ is the de-Broglie wavelength of the electron in the $n^{\text{th}}$ orbit,

$r_{n}$ is the radius of the $n^{\text{th}}$ orbit,

$n$ is the principal quantum number (which is 4 in this case).

According to Bohr's theory, the radius of the $n^{\text{th}}$ orbit is given by:

$r_{n}=n^{2}a_{0}$

where $a_{0}$ is the Bohr radius.

For the $4^{\text{th}}$ orbit, $n=4$, so the radius is:

$r_{4}=4^{2}a_{0}=16a_{0}$

Substituting $r_{4}$ into the de-Broglie wavelength formula, we get:

$λ_{4}=\frac{2π(16a_{0})}{4}=8πa_{0}$

text: The number of different chain isomers for C${}_{7}$H${}_{16}$ is $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
An alkane has no functional group, so the structural isomers of $\mathrm{C}{}_{7}\mathrm{H}{}_{16}$ can differ only in the carbon skeleton; every one of them is a chain isomer of the others.

Longest chain of 7 C: heptane (1).

Longest chain of 6 C: 2-methylhexane, 3-methylhexane (2).

Longest chain of 5 C: 2,2-dimethylpentane, 2,3-dimethylpentane, 2,4-dimethylpentane, 3,3-dimethylpentane, 3-ethylpentane (5).

Longest chain of 4 C: 2,2,3-trimethylbutane (1).

Names such as 2-ethylpentane or 2-ethyl-2-methylbutane are not new isomers; they describe 3-methylhexane and 3,3-dimethylpentane.

$\text{Total}=1+2+5+1=9$

Hence, the answer is 9.

text:
Consider the following reaction

$\mathrm{MnO}_{2}+\mathrm{KOH}+\mathrm{O}_{2}\to \mathrm{A}+\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}\text{.}$

Product '$\mathrm{A}$' in neutral or acidic medium disproportionate to give products '$\mathrm{B}$' and '$\mathrm{C}$' along with water. The sum of spin-only magnetic moment values of $\mathrm{B}$ and $\mathrm{C}$ is $________ BM. ($nearest integer) (Given atomic number of $\mathrm{Mn}$ is 25)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Fusion of $\mathrm{MnO}{}_{2}$ with KOH in air gives potassium manganate, so A is $\mathrm{K}{}_{2}\mathrm{MnO}{}_{4}$:

$2~\mathrm{MnO}{}_{2}+4\mathrm{KOH}+\mathrm{O}{}_{2}\longrightarrow 2\mathrm{K}{}_{2}\mathrm{MnO}{}_{4}+2\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

In neutral or acidic medium, manganate disproportionates:

$3~\mathrm{MnO}{}_{4}{}^{2-}+4\mathrm{H}{}^{+}\longrightarrow 2\mathrm{MnO}{}_{4}{}^{-}+\mathrm{MnO}{}_{2}+2\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

So B and C are $\mathrm{KMnO}{}_{4}$ (Mn +7, $3d^{0}$, $μ=0$) and $\mathrm{MnO}{}_{2}$ (Mn +4, $3d^{3}$, 3 unpaired electrons).

$μ(\mathrm{MnO}{}_{2})=\sqrt{3(3+2)}=\sqrt{15}=3.87\text{BM}$

Sum $=0+3.87=3.87$ BM, which is 4 to the nearest integer.

Hence, the answer is 4.
